text:
morgan: Heads-up — CI perf run showed repeated OOMs on paged-attn under mixed batch sizes. Traces point at KV cache churn + small workspace allocations causing allocator hot-path to thrash. Anyone seen similar?

nina: yep saw that earlier today on a different model. metrics: KV eviction rate spikes when ws < 8MB per stream, then compaction kicks in and latency ~2x.

jai: can you paste the trace? quick look at timeline would help.

morgan: sharing snippet from perf-run-193:
```
[1732109876] stream=0 model=xl25 seqlens={8..4096} batching=auto
alloc: request 1.2MB -> got slab-8kb, then backfill -> workspace growth to 12MB -> kv_cache_evict(src=prefix)
kernel selection: fallback to small-block kernel at t+120ms
OOM at t+127ms
```

nina: interesting — compaction starts because many tiny allocations prevent coalescing. the allocator then scans block pool which blocks the batcher.

perf-bot: perf summary (176s window): p99 latency +60%, token util -18%, gpu memory utilization oscillation 62%-91%.

morgan: hypothesis: our current "ws auto" picks minimal per-stream ws for low-latency short seqs, but when mixed workloads arrive it never grows fast enough and KV eviction preempts critical kernels. we should try: 1) aggressive pre-reserve for first N tokens, 2) KV eviction prioritization by prefix-freq, 3) early kernel fallback threshold.

jai: +1 for pre-reserve. small experiment idea: bump min_ws to 16MB for 10% of capacity for one minute, measure evict rate and kernel fallbacks. can do a canary on a quarter of the podset.

nina: also propose a lightweight KV hot-index: mark entries touched in last 500ms as hot and bias eviction toward cold partitions — cheaper than compaction.

morgan: config I'm thinking of (quick):
```json
{
  "workspace": {"min_bytes": 16777216, "growth_policy": "predictive", "predictive_window_ms": 200},
  "kv_cache": {"hot_window_ms": 500, "evict_policy": "coldest_first_by_access", "max_evictions_per_ms": 4},
  "kernel": {"fallback_latency_ms": 80, "prefer_fast_kernel_on_miss": true}
}
```

perf-bot: canary job scheduled: run-id=canary-1732110001 target=podset-beta. will collect kv_evictions, ws_growth, kernel_switch_count.

ops-bot: canary started on 3 nodes @1732110005. routing: 10% traffic split.

jai: quick question — how do we measure compaction cost precisely? I want to compare compaction CPU time vs wasted allocation overhead.

nina: add these counters to kv: compaction_time_ms, compaction_bytes_moved, compaction_ops. Also workspace_fragmentation_pct calculated as 1 - (largest_free_contig / total_free).

morgan: added to the canary metrics list. also capturing 'kernel_fallback_reason' tag (oom|frag|slow_alloc).

perf-bot: 60s into canary: observed kv_evictions -= 38%, kernel_fallback_count -= 24%, p99 latency down 18% vs baseline. ws growth events +12% but no OOMs so far.

jai: promising. what about compaction_time?

perf-bot: compaction_time_ms increased 9% but compaction_bytes_moved decreased 41% (fewer aggressive sweeps). net CPU up ~2%.

nina: that's acceptable tradeoff. fewer heavy compactions means less blocking on allocator path.

morgan: note: we still see occasional microbursts when many medium-length seqs arrive — KV hot index helps but we might need microbatching guarding (limit concurrent small-block allocations when batcher sees >X inflight).

jai: implement microbatch guard: if inflight_short_streams > 20 then throttle accepting new short streams for 50ms. cheap to add in batcher.

ops-bot: microbatch guard patch rolled to canary @1732110302.

perf-bot: final canary summary (6m): p99 -22%, evictions -45%, kernel fallback -30%, compaction_time +6%, no OOMs. CPU +3%.

morgan: nice. next steps: 1) ship min_ws bump and kv-hot eviction to beta with 25% rollout, 2) monitor compaction_time and latency, 3) follow-up to explore async compaction off-main-path. I'll draft a PR with configs and perf graphs.

nina: I'll open the KV-hot PR and add metrics.

jai: I'll do the batcher throttle change and add unit tests for inflight_short_streams counter.

morgan: thanks all. if anyone wants the raw traces I pushed them to s3://redwood-perf/canary/1732110001/ — cc @everyone :thumbsup:

perf-bot: archived canary artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/canary/1732110001/summary.json

morgan: closing thread, will update when beta rollout starts.
